Second Reading of the Road Traffic (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill

Second Reading4 August 2026 bill-803, bill-804, bill-802

A Bill at Second Reading, moved by the Second Minister for Home Affairs on behalf of the Senior Minister, amending the Road Traffic Act to strengthen penalties for dangerous driving, tighten alcohol limits, create a drug-driving offence, and enhance enforcement.

The Bill creates a new offence of purposeful endangerment carrying up to 15 years' imprisonment and lifetime disqualification, lowers the prescribed alcohol limits, makes holding a mobile phone while a vehicle is in motion an offence, and introduces a presence-based drug-driving offence. It also allows automated notices for traffic offences and tightens the Driver Improvement Points System from January 2027.

  • Ms Sim Ann

    • The Second Minister moved that the Bill be read a Second time.

      Verbatim
      That the Bill be now read a Second time.

    • The Bill has three objectives: strengthen accountability for the most egregious road conduct, further deter driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs, and enhance the Traffic Police's ability to detect and enforce against traffic offences.

      Verbatim
      to achieve three key objectives: First, strengthen accountability for the most egregious road conduct; Second, further deter driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs; and third, enhance the Traffic Police's ability to detect and enforce against traffic offences.

    • Clause 6 introduces a new offence of purposeful endangerment.

      Verbatim
      Clause 6, therefore, introduces a new offence of purposeful endangerment.

    • Where death is caused under the purposeful endangerment offence, the offender may be imprisoned up to 15 years and is liable to fine or caning, or both.

      Verbatim
      Where death is caused, the offender is to be punished with imprisonment, which may extend to 15 years and is also liable to fine or caning, or both.

    • The Court must impose lifetime driving disqualification for purposeful endangerment unless there are special reasons, in which case at least 10 years' disqualification applies.

      Verbatim
      The Court must also impose driving disqualification for life, unless there are special reasons not to do so; and if special reasons apply, the Court must impose at least 10 years of driving disqualification.

    • The Bill increases the maximum imprisonment for dangerous driving causing grievous hurt from five to seven years for first-time offenders and from 10 to 13 years for repeat offenders.

      Verbatim
      the Bill increases the maximum imprisonment term for first-time offenders from five years to seven years, and for repeat offenders from 10 years to 13 years.

    • The maximum additional imprisonment uplift for serious offenders increases from one year to one and a half years.

      Verbatim
      the maximum uplift for serious offenders will increase from one year to one and a half years' imprisonment.

    • The Bill tightens prescribed alcohol limits from exceeding 35 microgrammes to 15 microgrammes per 100 millilitres of breath, and from exceeding 80 milligrammes to 30 milligrammes per 100 millilitres of blood.

      Verbatim
      tighten the prescribed alcohol limits from exceeding 35 microgrammes of alcohol in 100 millilitres of breath, to 15 microgrammes of alcohol in 100 millilitres of breath; and from exceeding 80 milligrammes of alcohol per 100 millilitres of blood, to 30 milligrammes of alcohol per 100 millilitres of blood.

    • Clause 11 introduces a new offence of driving or attempting to drive with a specified substance present in blood, without separately proving impairment.

      Verbatim
      Clause 11 therefore introduces a new offence under the new section 67(1)(c) of the RTA, where a person who drives or attempts to drive with the presence of a specified substance in his blood will commit an offence, without separately proving that he was impaired whilst driving.

    • A statutory defence applies where the substance was lawfully consumed or administered and the person did not know or have reason to believe it could impair driving.

      Verbatim
      The Bill provides a statutory defence where the substance was lawfully consumed by or administered; and the person did not know or have reason to believe that consuming it could impair his or her driving.

    • Clause 14 removes the requirement to administer a preliminary breath test, streamlining drink-driving enforcement.

      Verbatim
      clause 14 of the Bill removes the requirement to administer a preliminary breath test, streamlining the drink-driving enforcement process.

    • Clause 16 removes the authorisation requirement for taking blood specimens from hospital patients under the RTA, aligning it with the Criminal Procedure Code.

      Verbatim
      Clause 16 therefore removes the authorisation requirement under the RTA, aligning it with the Criminal Procedure Code provisions.

    • Clause 10 amends section 65B so that holding a mobile communication device while the vehicle is in motion is an offence, without needing to prove the driver was operating it.

      Verbatim
      Clause 10 therefore amends section 65B to remove the element stating that the driver must be operating the device. A driver who holds a mobile communication device in his hand while the vehicle is in motion will commit an offence.

    • Touching a device secured in a mount while driving is not an offence.

      Verbatim
      This amendment also makes clear that it is not an offence if the device is secured in a mount and a driver touches it while driving.

    • Clause 21 introduces section 81A, allowing a computer program to assess evidence and automatically issue a notice requiring the vehicle owner to provide the driver's particulars.

      Verbatim
      Clause 21 introduces a new section 81A, which allows a computer program to assess whether there is sufficient evidence that a traffic offence was committed and if so, automatically issue a notice to require the vehicle owner to provide the particulars of the driver at the time of the alleged offence.

    • The Bill amends provisions to make clear how driving disqualification periods are calculated.

      Verbatim
      First, the Bill amends a number of provisions in the RTA to make clear how driving disqualification periods are calculated.

    • The Driver Improvement Points System will be tightened from January 2027, lowering the suspension threshold from 24 to 18 demerit points and lengthening suspension periods.

      Verbatim
      we announced last week that we will tighten the Driver Improvement Points System, commonly known as the demerit points regime, to be implemented from January 2027. The two key changes are the lowering of the suspension threshold from 24 demerit points to 18 and lengthening the suspension periods for errant drivers who meet this lowered threshold.

      Verbatim
      My question is whether this is necessary as I believe such a person can probably be prosecuted under existing offences where such a person can be charged for intending to cause death or grievous hurt under the Penal Code.

  • Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)

    • Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong supported the introduction of penalties for purposeful endangerment, tightened alcohol limits, the standalone drug driving framework, and automated enforcement.

      Verbatim
      I fully support the introduction of penalties for purposeful endangerment, the tightening of legal alcohol limits, the standalone drug driving framework and the transition towards automated enforcement technology.

  • Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)

    • Dr Wan Rizal asked the Ministry to commit to a review in a few years.

      Verbatim
      I would ask the Ministry to commit to a review in a few years.

Parliament moves to revise terms of service for Parliament staff

4 August 2026 motion-3006

A motion moved by the Leader of the House asking Parliament to determine that the terms of service of Parliament staff under the Parliamentary Scheme (2008) and the Language Executive Scheme (Parliament) (2008) be revised in line with the Report of the Commission on Parliament Staff.

The transcript states that Parliament staff on these two schemes will receive the same salary adjustments of 2% to 9% given to civil servants on the Management Executive Scheme (2008), with effect from 1 August 2026. It also states that a retention payment component will be introduced for Parliamentary Clerks with effect from 1 September 2026. The stated aim is to keep the terms of service of Parliament staff competitive in attracting and retaining officers.

  • The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)

    • The Leader of the House moved that Parliament determine that the terms of service of Parliament staff be revised in accordance with paragraph 12 of the Commission's Report.

      Verbatim
      That this Parliament determines that the terms of service of the staff of Parliament under the Parliamentary Scheme (2008) and the Language Executive Scheme (Parliament) (2008) shall be revised in accordance with paragraph 12 of the Report of the Commission on Parliament Staff in Paper Misc 4 of 2026

    • The Commission presented its Report to Parliament on 27 July 2026.

      Verbatim
      The Commission presented its Report to Parliament on 27 July 2026.

    • Civil servants on the Management Executive Scheme (2008) were announced to receive salary adjustments of 2% to 9%.

      Verbatim
      On 20 February 2026, the Public Service Division (PSD) announced that eligible civil servants on the Management Executive Scheme (2008) would receive salary adjustments of 2% to 9% to keep pace with market standards and enable the Public Service to continue to attract and retain talent to deliver well for Singaporeans.

    • Those civil service adjustments took effect on 1 August 2026.

      Verbatim
      These adjustments took effect on 1 August 2026.

    • The Commission recommends that the two Parliament staff schemes adopt the same salary adjustments, also from 1 August 2026.

      Verbatim
      The Commission recommends that the Parliamentary Scheme (2008) and Language Executive Scheme (Parliament) (2008) adopt the same salary adjustments, also with effect from 1 August 2026.

    • The Commission recommends a retention payment component for Parliamentary Clerks taking effect from 1 September 2026.

      Verbatim
      The Commission also recommends introducing a retention payment component for Parliamentary Clerks under the Parliamentary Scheme (2008), and for this to take effect from 1 September 2026.

    • The Public Service Division supports the proposals.

      Verbatim
      PSD supports these proposals.

    • The Leader of the House asked the House to accept the Commission's recommendations.

      Verbatim
      I ask the House to accept the recommendations of the Commission.

  • Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)

    • Ms Jessica Tan rose in support of the Motion.

      Verbatim
      I rise in support of the Motion moved by the Leader of the House.

    • The retention payment is described as having a fixed quantum of roughly 1.5 to 1.75 months' salary per year.

      Verbatim
      a fixed quantum, roughly equivalent to 1.5 to 1.75 months' salary per year

    • The retention payment is described as including annual payouts for entry level Clerks, three-year payouts for those recognised for competence capped at 20 years, and a one-off ex-gratia payment to support the transition.

      Verbatim
      annual payouts for entry level Clerks and three-year payouts for those recognised for competence, but capped at 20 years, and a one-off ex-gratia payment to support the transition

    • Ms Jessica Tan said recruitment has become more challenging, especially for legally trained officers.

      Verbatim
      Recruitment has also become more challenging, especially for legally trained officers who can handle the specialised nature of Parliamentary work.

  • Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)

    • Mr Christopher de Souza rose in firm support of the Report.

      Verbatim
      I rise in firm support of the Report of the Commission on Parliament Staff

    • Mr Christopher de Souza described the Report as comprising adoption of the PSD adjustments for the Management Executive Scheme plus higher discretionary bonuses, and a retention payment component.

      Verbatim
      first, adopting the same adjustments adopted by PSD for the Management Executive Scheme, as well as higher discretionary bonuses to recognise and encourage strong performance. Second, introducing a retention payment component to attract and retain talent, as set out in paragraph 10 of the Report.

    • Mr Christopher de Souza urged all Members to support the Motion unanimously.

      Verbatim
      I urge all Members to support this worthy Motion unanimously.

  • The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)

    • The Leader of the House thanked the two Members for their support and urged Members to support the Motion.

      Verbatim
      I do not think there is anything further I need to say in response, other than to thank Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Christopher de Souza for their strong support for the Motion and also to urge Members of the House to support the Motion.

Adjournment speech on public transport: bus contracting, rail financing and autonomous vehicles

4 August 2026 matter-adj-3007

An adjournment motion moved by the Deputy Leader of the House, followed by an adjournment speech by Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis setting out proposals on buses, rail and autonomous vehicles, and a response from the Senior Minister of State for Transport, Ms Sun Xueling.

The transcript sets out planned changes to public transport: the rail network is to grow from 275 kilometres today to about 360 kilometres by the early 2030s, and more than half of bus services now run at intervals of 10 minutes or less during peak. Six autonomous buses have been procured and are due to start operating on Bus Services 400 and 191 in the second half of 2026.

  • The Deputy Leader of the House (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)

    • The Deputy Leader of the House moved that Parliament adjourn.

      Verbatim
      I seek to move, "That Parliament do now adjourn."

  • Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)

    • Mr Chua said the Land Transport Authority aims for 75% of peak hour journeys by public transport by 2030, and that the figure was 66% in financial year 2024.

      Verbatim
      the LTA aims to have 75% of all peak hour journeys carried out via public transport by 2030

    • Mr Chua said the proportion of local bus captains fell from 54% to 41% between 2021 and 2025.

      Verbatim
      From 2021 to 2025, the proportion of local bus captains dropped from 54% to 41%

    • Mr Chua asked whether bus scheduled headways could be set at 10 minutes or less.

      Verbatim
      Can we aim for a shorter scheduled headway of 10 minutes or less, period?

    • Mr Chua cited the Tampines bus package award to Go-Ahead Group at $646 million over an incumbent bid of $596 million.

      Verbatim
      the LTA awarded the contract to the Go-Ahead Group, the company that placed the highest bids, for $646 million instead of offering it to the incumbent operator who placed the lowest bid of $596 million

    • Mr Chua asked the Government to accelerate tendering for the remaining four of 14 bus packages never put up for competitive tender.

      Verbatim
      I hope that the Government can accelerate the calling of tenders for the remaining four of 14 bus packages that have never been put up for competitive tender

    • Mr Chua proposed publishing bus operator performance data annually.

      Verbatim
      Publishing this annually, as Transport for London does quarterly, would cost nothing additional

    • Mr Chua called for a renewed rail financing framework converging all lines onto a single service-fee framework and consolidating rail operations under a single publicly owned national rail operator.

      Verbatim
      I therefore call for a renewed rail financing framework: to complete the convergence of all rail lines onto a single, unified service-fee framework, and go one step further by consolidating rail operations under a single, publicly owned national rail operator.

    • Mr Chua said AV roll-out remains largely in the trial phase, with around 20 AVs on short fixed routes in Punggol.

      Verbatim
      our AV roll-out remains largely in the trial phase, with only around 20 AVs involved in short, fixed route services in Punggol

    • Mr Chua said six autonomous buses were procured at $8 million and are due to operate on Bus Services 400 and 191 in the second half of 2026.

      Verbatim
      We also have six autonomous buses procured at a contract value of $8 million, due to start operating on Bus Services 400 and 191 in the second half of 2026.

    • Mr Chua asked the Ministry of Transport to provide numerical targets for its AV ambition.

      Verbatim
      can the MOT provide numerical targets for our AV ambition

  • The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Ms Sun Xueling)

    • Ms Sun said the Government's ambition is 75% peak-period public transport mode share.

      Verbatim
      Our ambition to achieve 75% peak-period mode share reflects this.

    • Ms Sun said about $2 billion a year is spent on public transport operating costs.

      Verbatim
      We invest heavily in our public transport system, about $2 billion a year on public transport operating costs

    • Ms Sun said the rail network will grow from 275 kilometres today to about 360 kilometres by the early 2030s.

      Verbatim
      we are growing the rail network from 275 kilometres today to about 360 kilometres by the early 2030s

    • Ms Sun said station locations for Phase 3 of the Cross Island Line were announced the previous week, and that travel to and from the West can be cut by up to 50 minutes.

      Verbatim
      Just last week, we announced the station locations for Phase 3 of the Cross Island Line.

    • Ms Sun said 11 new City Direct Services have been rolled out under the Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme since 2024.

      Verbatim
      We have rolled out 11 new City Direct Services since we started the Bus Connectivity Enhancement Programme in 2024

    • Ms Sun said service fees paid by the Government to bus operators have dropped by 15% since tendering out bus packages.

      Verbatim
      Since we transited to tendering out bus packages, service fees paid by the Government to the operators have dropped by 15%.

    • Ms Sun said bus contracts are awarded through a two-envelope process considering quality first, then price.

      Verbatim

    • Ms Sun said the Government is working with operators to attract more bus captains by raising starting salaries.

  • Mr Speaker

What happens next The Senior Minister of State said the Rail Reliability Taskforce recommendations are being implemented with more updates to come, and that the Government is working towards an AV Act. The Speaker said the sitting the next day would commence at 10.30 am, and Parliament adjourned at 8.15 pm.

How this page was made

Built from the official Hansard record (Parliament of Singapore Official Reports). No news reporting was used. Briefs are written by software from the transcript and every key point carries the verbatim words it was drawn from.

  • Reports collected: 200 (complete)
  • Briefs on this page: 3 (87 verified points)
  • Speaker attribution: 98% of turns carry an explicit speaker tag
  • Any point whose quote could not be found in the transcript was discarded rather than shown.
